To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

RNA editing in intron 6 of the astroglial glutamate transporter EAAT2 activates a cryptic alternative 3′ polyadenylation site and is associated with intron 7 inclusion in the mature transcript, which is significantly increased in ALS spinal cord and motor cortex.

(i) RNA editing activates a cryptic alternative 3' polyadenylation site in intron seven of the EAAT2 pre mRNA, (ii) this site includes two overlapping strong polyadenylation signals in a conserved strong stem loop, (iii) RNA editing is significantly higher in spinal and motor cortex from ALS patients, (iv) RNA editing and polyadenyation in intron 3 are strongly correlated, (v) RNA editing releases the alternative polyadenyation signal

(i) RNA editing at a specific site in the pre-mRNA of the EAAT2 glutamatergic transporter activates a cryptic alternative intronic polyadenylation site; (ii) this polyadenylation site is conserved in primata; and (iii) RNA editing is increased in the spinal cord and motor cortex from ALS patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of alternative splicing in EAAT2, a gene that is implicated in ALS.
the aberrant expression of EAAT2, a key glutamate transporter in the brain, and its potential role in motor neurone disease.
a previously unknown mechanism for the regulation of pre-mRNA polyadenylation by RNA editing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increased RNA editing in the EAAT2 gene in ALS is a consequence of the aberrant splicing of intron 7 and the increased production of the intron 7 inclusion isoform.
RNA editing in intron 2 of EAAT2 is a novel mechanism for the aberrant splicing of this gene, and that it may contribute to the pathology of ALS.
the editing of EAAT2 mRNA in the CNS of ALS patients leads to the activation of a cryptic alternative splicing site and the generation of a truncated protein, which is not functional.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
increased RNA editing in ALS patients activates a cryptic alternative 3′ polyadenylation site in the EAAT2 intron 7.
RNA editing in EA2T2 pre-mRNA activates an alternative polyadenyltion signal, generating intron retention transcripts, which are significantly increased in ALS patients.
RNA editing in the intron of EAAT2 is increased in ALS patients and that this editing may be involved in the aberrant intron inclusion in the EAAT2 pre mRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
increased RNA editing in EA2T2 intron 7 may be a key factor in ALS pathogenesis.
the editing event is a prerequisite for the alternative polyadenylations, suggesting that the editing site may be an important target for the development of novel therapies for ALS.
RNA editing can activate an alternative polyadenylated site, generating aberrant RNA transcripts that may contribute to the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases.
